output_units.text: Open Control Panel → Power Options → Change plan settings → Change advanced power settings. Set Wireless Adapter Settings → Power Saving Mode to Maximum Performance for both On battery and Plugged in. output_units.normalized_text: step 1 clear the drain opening remove the sink strainer or stopper if present. pull out visible food sludge with a paper towel or gloved fingers. clean around the drain mouth.
output_units.text: Step 1 | Clear the drain opening | Remove the sink strainer or stopper if present. Pull out visible food sludge with a paper towel or gloved fingers. Clean around the drain mouth.

output_units.normalized_text: step 2 dish soap plus hot water add a generous squirt of dish soap. run very hot tap water for 2-3 minutes or pour a kettle or pot of hot but not boiling water in stages if you have pvc plumbing. best for soft grease buildup.
output_units.text: Step 2 | Dish soap plus hot water | Add a generous squirt of dish soap. Run very hot tap water for 2-3 minutes, or pour a kettle or pot of hot but not boiling water in stages if you have PVC plumbing. Best for soft grease buildup.

output_units.normalized_text: step 3 baking soda plus vinegar pour in about 1/2 cup baking soda then 1 cup white vinegar. let sit 10-15 minutes. flush with hot water. this is modestly helpful for light residue do not expect miracles on a heavy clog.
output_units.text: Step 3 | Baking soda plus vinegar | Pour in about 1/2 cup baking soda, then 1 cup white vinegar. Let sit 10-15 minutes. Flush with hot water. This is modestly helpful for light residue; do not expect miracles on a heavy clog.

output_units.normalized_text: step 4 plunge the sink if double-basin seal the other basin with a wet rag or stopper. add enough water to cover the plunger lip. use a sink plunger for 20-30 firm strokes. flush with hot water and test drainage.
output_units.text: Step 4 | Plunge the sink | If double-basin, seal the other basin with a wet rag or stopper. Add enough water to cover the plunger lip. Use a sink plunger for 20-30 firm strokes. Flush with hot water and test drainage.

output_units.normalized_text: step 5 check the dishwasher basics look under the sink for a kinked dishwasher drain hose. make sure the hose loops upward before connecting to the drain or disposal inlet if visible. if you have a garbage disposal and it was recently installed or replaced the dishwasher knockout plug could be relevant but that usually causes more immediate dishwasher drainage issues than a 2-week slow sink.
output_units.text: Step 5 | Check the dishwasher basics | Look under the sink for a kinked dishwasher drain hose. Make sure the hose loops upward before connecting to the drain or disposal inlet if visible. If you have a garbage disposal and it was recently installed or replaced, the dishwasher knockout plug could be relevant, but that usually causes more immediate dishwasher drainage issues than a 2-week slow sink.

output_units.normalized_text: step 6 clean the disposal splash guard if you have a disposal with power off at the switch wipe under the rubber guard. run cold water and briefly operate the disposal if it sounds normal. do not put hands into the grinding chamber.
output_units.text: Step 6 | Clean the disposal splash guard, if you have a disposal | With power off at the switch, wipe under the rubber guard. Run cold water and briefly operate the disposal if it sounds normal. Do not put hands into the grinding chamber.
